title: Two Sum
summary: You get a list of integers `nums` and an integer `target`. Exactly one pair of different positions holds values that add up to `target`. Return those two positions, in any order.
constraints: exactly one pair adds up to target
a position cannot be used twice

approaches.twist: Store each value's index; before storing x, look up target minus x.

approaches.note: Works, but checking every pair takes O(n²) time. The target is O(n).

signals.meaning: For each value, the partner you need is target minus that value.
You need indexes, so remember where each value was.

signals.phrase: a position cannot be used twice
signals.meaning: Look up the partner before storing the current value.

constraintReading: len(nums) up to 10⁴ makes O(n²) about 10⁸ steps, too slow to be comfortable, so aim for O(n) with extra memory.

hints.clarify: Can the same position be used twice? Try [6, 6] with target 12 by hand: which two positions answer it?
hints.approach: Walk the list once. For each value, the partner it needs is target minus the value; a dict from value to index answers "have I seen it?" in O(1).
hints.whyNot: Sorting and two pointers finds the values but loses their original positions.

slots.setup: An empty dict from value to index.
slots.loop: Go over every index and value.
slots.update: Work out the partner: target minus the value.
slots.record: If the partner is stored, return both indexes; otherwise store the value's index.
slots.return: The problem promises a pair, so the loop always returns.

solution.explanation: Each value is looked up and stored once, so the time is O(n). The dict holds up to n entries, so the space is O(n).

related.relation: Also a hash map, but it counts letters instead of remembering positions.
